content: I know that taking more than about half a dozen tons a day can tip the balance when others also take, so I’ll aim for six tons today to keep income going but not overexploiting, and I’ll stay on the water tomorrow to see how the fish respond and whether others will pull harder, and when I get back to the dock I’ll ask the others what they plan to take today so we can avoid over‑exploiting.
Intended to say: others: to ask what they plan to take today to avoid over‑exploiting.

I want a moderate catch and not to tip the balance; knowing others’ numbers will help me decide whether to stay or head back early.

That is the amount I normally aim for – enough to keep income going but not enough to push the fish stock down when others are also fishing. Since the others caught nothing, it suggests the fish are still abundant. I have no reason to suspect they will suddenly go over the limit. I can still take my usual amount if I go out, and the lake can handle it. I’ll keep an eye on the others and the lake’s response.
You headed straight out to fish and missed the dock conversation.
Harvests this round: Ana=12t, Marco=10t, Sofia=0t, James=0t, Yuki=6t. Lake now at 138.1t. At dock: Sofia, James. Out fishing: Ana, Marco, Yuki.
I’ll cut back to four tons today to reduce cumulative pressure on the lake, and I’ll stay out tomorrow to observe fish response and see if Ana or Marco change plans.

I’ve been keeping the lake on a tight budget after the last round’s 22‑ton haul, and the stock is already down to 124.2 tons. Four tons is a safe level that keeps my income steady without adding extra pressure when Sofia and Yuki are docked and likely to catch.

That’s a big hit, and the lake has already been declining. I’ve been cutting back to four tons whenever the stock dips. Given the current numbers and the fact that I’m not catching this round, I’m going to stay at the dock tomorrow and let the others take their share.

I’ve been cutting back to four tons when the lake is dropping, and I’ve kept myself at the dock during the sharpest declines to let the others take the load. If I go out tomorrow, I’d probably take only four tons at best, and I’d still be adding to a lake that’s already lower than it was a few rounds ago. It seems safer to stay at the dock again and let Marco, Sofia, and Yuki take their share, then decide next round whether to come back out.

My own harvest has been 4 t when the stock is that low, and that keeps the total removal within a range that has historically allowed the lake to recover over the following rounds. I prefer to wait and see how the stock behaves after their 14 t haul before deciding whether to take a catch.

I have no incentive to increase the harvest this round, and I can use the dock to monitor what Ana and Sofia do and see if they change their plans. Staying also gives me a chance to speak with Sofia about cutting her haul if she’s willing to aim for a lower total, which would benefit the lake and keep our future income steadier.
